The main takeaway from our work is that
the equation of state of SU(N) gauge theories in 2+1 dimensions can be accurately computed in the confining and deconfining phases.
the thermodynamics in the confining regime is well described by a gas with a small number of glueballs, which are not too heavy and whose spectrum is accurately predicted by a bosonic string model.

, in 2 > + 3 dimensions, SU(N) Yang–Mills theories are characterized by the same qualitative features as their 3 + 1 dimensional counterparts, namely a confining phase and a deconfining phase, with a first-order phase transition in-between.
